review_output.summary: Re-raising the first child's error means the callers' cleanup never runs: `ensure_kv_transfer_shutdown` never sets `_KV_CONNECTOR_AGENT = None`, and `EngineCore.shutdown` gets an exception from `scheduler.shutdown()`.
review_output.failure_scenario: One child connector's `shutdown()` raises during worker teardown. `kv_transfer_state.ensure_kv_transfer_shutdown` stops at `_KV_CONNECTOR_AGENT.shutdown()` and skips `_KV_CONNECTOR_AGENT = None`, so the global keeps pointing at a half-shut-down MultiConnector. A later shutdown call, e.g. from `__del__` or atexit, runs `shutdown()` on every child again, which can double-free or raise again. On the scheduler side, `Scheduler.shutdown` and then `EngineCore.shutdown` get the exception with nothing to catch it, so engine teardown aborts with a traceback instead of finishing.

review_output.summary: Only `exceptions[0]` is raised; every later child failure is dropped from the raised error.
review_output.failure_scenario: Two child connectors fail with different errors. The caller, or any test that uses `pytest.raises`, sees only the first. The second is visible only in the logs, so tests and monitoring can miss it. An aggregated error such as a RuntimeError listing all failures, chained with `from`, would keep all of them.

review_output.summary: `logger.exception(..., str(e))` prints the error text twice, because `logger.exception` already appends the traceback and message.
review_output.failure_scenario: Each failed child shutdown logs its message twice, in the formatted line and again in the traceback. It is just noise; `logger.exception("Exception during connector %s shutdown.", c.__class__.__name__)` is enough.

review_output.summary: Adding `shutdown` only to MultiConnector does not reach real cleanup for its most common child: NixlConnector does not override `shutdown()` and still cleans up in `NixlConnectorWorker.__del__` (nixl_connector.py:554), so the loop calls the base class's do-nothing method.
review_output.failure_scenario: A MultiConnector wrapping NixlConnector plus another connector is shut down. `c.shutdown()` on the Nixl child does nothing, so `_handshake_initiation_executor` and the NIXL agent resources are not released at shutdown. Cleanup still depends on GC timing, which is the problem this PR set out to fix. The underlying fix is to implement `shutdown()` in the child connectors, starting with NixlConnector.

review_output.summary: No test covers the new `shutdown` fan-out, the continue-after-failure behaviour, or the re-raise.
review_output.failure_scenario: A later regression could go unnoticed, e.g. shutting down only the first connector, stopping after the first exception, or swallowing errors. There is also no check that every child's `shutdown()` is called when an earlier one raises.
